images.title: Four circled numbers
images.purpose: Show four numbers circled in different rows and columns of a 4 by 4 grid, and their sum.
images.composition: Small 4 by 4 grid on top, number row centred below with wide space.
images.exact_structure: A 4 by 4 grid of 16 equal empty cells with grey #6B7280 outlines. Exactly 4 cells carry a teal #0072B2 circle: row 1 column 1, row 2 column 3, row 3 column 4, row 4 column 2, so no two share a row or column. Below, one row of the 4 circled numbers 3, −5, 7, −6 in order. Exactly 16 cells, 4 circles, 1 number row.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
two circles in the same row or column
numbers written inside the grid cells
images.takeaway: Add the circled numbers one at a time, keeping every sign, to get −1.
images.description: A 4 by 4 grid with four teal circles, one in each row and each column, and the number row 3, −5, 7, −6 adding to −1.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to say why no two circles share a row or column, then add the four numbers.

image_decisions.why: The circle and strike game is a picture idea; one clean grid carries it.
